questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The stored charge in the capacitor in steady state of the following circuit is ________ $\mu$C.
questions.solution:
In steady state, the capacitor acts as an open circuit, meaning no current flows through the branch containing the $100\ \mu\text{F}$ capacitor. Consequently, no current flows through the $10\ \Omega$ resistor in series with it on the top right.

The voltage across the capacitor will be equal to the voltage across the $4\ \Omega$ vertical resistor.

Let's simplify the circuit to find this voltage. The $12\ \Omega$ resistor on the left is in parallel with the $12\ \text{V}$ battery, so the voltage across the rest of the circuit remains $12\ \text{V}$.

For the rightmost part of the active circuit, the $4\ \Omega$ top resistor, the $4\ \Omega$ vertical resistor, and the $2\ \Omega$ bottom resistor are in series. Their equivalent resistance is:
$R_{\text{right}} = 4\ \Omega + 4\ \Omega + 2\ \Omega = 10\ \Omega$

This $10\ \Omega$ equivalent resistance is in parallel with the $10\ \Omega$ vertical resistor in the middle. The equivalent resistance of this parallel combination is:
$R_{\text{mid}} = \dfrac{10 \times 10}{10 + 10} = 5\ \Omega$

Now, the total resistance of the main circuit connected to the $12\ \text{V}$ source is the sum of the $5\ \Omega$ top-left resistor, the $5\ \Omega$ equivalent middle resistance, and the $2\ \Omega$ bottom-left resistor:
$R_{\text{total}} = 5\ \Omega + 5\ \Omega + 2\ \Omega = 12\ \Omega$

The total current flowing from the $12\ \text{V}$ source into this main branch is:
$I = \dfrac{12\ \text{V}}{12\ \Omega} = 1\ \text{A}$

The voltage across the parallel combination (the middle section) is:
$V_{\text{mid}} = I \times R_{\text{mid}} = 1\ \text{A} \times 5\ \Omega = 5\ \text{V}$

This $5\ \text{V}$ is applied across the right branch which has a total resistance of $10\ \Omega$. The current through this branch is:
$I_{\text{right}} = \dfrac{5\ \text{V}}{10\ \Omega} = 0.5\ \text{A}$

The voltage across the $4\ \Omega$ vertical resistor is:
$V_{4\Omega} = I_{\text{right}} \times 4\ \Omega = 0.5\ \text{A} \times 4\ \Omega = 2\ \text{V}$

Since the capacitor is in parallel with this $4\ \Omega$ resistor (with no voltage drop across the $10\ \Omega$ resistor in its branch), the voltage across the capacitor is also $2\ \text{V}$.

The stored charge in the capacitor is:
$Q = C \times V = 100\ \mu\text{F} \times 2\ \text{V} = 200\ \mu\text{C}$

Answer: $200$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A moving coil of galvanometer when shunted with $2\,\Omega$ resistance gives a full scale deflection for a current of $500$ mA. When a resistance of $470\,\Omega$ is connected in series it gives a full scale deflection for $10$ V potential applied on it. The value of resistance of galvanometer coil is __________ $\Omega$.
questions.solution:
Let $G$ be the resistance of the galvanometer and $I_g$ be the current required for full scale deflection.

When the galvanometer is shunted with $S = 2\,\Omega$, it acts as an ammeter of range $I = 500\text{ mA} = 0.5\text{ A}$. The potential difference across the galvanometer and the shunt is equal:

$I_g G = (I - I_g) S$

$I_g G = (0.5 - I_g) \times 2$

$I_g G + 2 I_g = 1$

$I_g = \dfrac{1}{G + 2}$

When a resistance $R = 470\,\Omega$ is connected in series, it acts as a voltmeter of range $V = 10\text{ V}$. The total voltage is the sum of the voltage drops:

$V = I_g (G + R)$

$10 = I_g (G + 470)$

$I_g = \dfrac{10}{G + 470}$

Equating the two expressions for $I_g$:

$\dfrac{1}{G + 2} = \dfrac{10}{G + 470}$

$G + 470 = 10(G + 2)$

$G + 470 = 10G + 20$

$9G = 450$

$G = 50\,\Omega$

Answer: $50$

questions.q: Two cells of emfs $1$ V and $2$ V and internal resistance $2\,\Omega$ and $1\,\Omega$, respectively connected in parallel, gave a current of $1$ A through an external resistance. If the polarity of one cell is reversed, then value of current through the external resistance will be $\dfrac{\alpha}{5}$ A. The value of $\alpha$ is __________.
questions.solution:
For two cells connected in parallel with the same polarity, the equivalent emf $E_{eq}$ and equivalent internal resistance $r_{eq}$ are given by:

$E_{eq} = \dfrac{E_1 r_2 + E_2 r_1}{r_1 + r_2}$

$r_{eq} = \dfrac{r_1 r_2}{r_1 + r_2}$

Substituting the given values ($E_1 = 1$ V, $r_1 = 2\,\Omega$, $E_2 = 2$ V, $r_2 = 1\,\Omega$):

$E_{eq} = \dfrac{1 \times 1 + 2 \times 2}{2 + 1} = \dfrac{5}{3}$ V

$r_{eq} = \dfrac{2 \times 1}{2 + 1} = \dfrac{2}{3}\,\Omega$

The current $I$ through the external resistance $R$ is $1$ A:

$I = \dfrac{E_{eq}}{R + r_{eq}}$

$1 = \dfrac{\dfrac{5}{3}}{R + \dfrac{2}{3}}$

$R + \dfrac{2}{3} = \dfrac{5}{3} \Rightarrow R = 1\,\Omega$

When the polarity of one cell is reversed, the new equivalent emf $E'_{eq}$ becomes:

$E'_{eq} = \dfrac{|E_1 r_2 - E_2 r_1|}{r_1 + r_2} = \dfrac{|1 \times 1 - 2 \times 2|}{3} = \dfrac{3}{3} = 1$ V

The equivalent internal resistance remains the same, $r_{eq} = \dfrac{2}{3}\,\Omega$.

The new current $I'$ through the external resistance $R$ is:

$I' = \dfrac{E'_{eq}}{R + r_{eq}} = \dfrac{1}{1 + \dfrac{2}{3}} = \dfrac{1}{\dfrac{5}{3}} = \dfrac{3}{5}$ A

Given that the new current is $\dfrac{\alpha}{5}$ A, we have:

$\dfrac{\alpha}{5} = \dfrac{3}{5} \Rightarrow \alpha = 3$

Answer: $3$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Refer to the circuit diagram given below. The heat generated across the $6\,\Omega$ resistance in $100$ second is $\dfrac{\alpha}{100}$ J. The value of $\alpha$ is _______. (Nearest integer)
questions.solution:
Taking the right-hand wire as the reference node at $0\text{ V}$, let the left junction (where the $3\,\Omega$, $4\,\Omega$ and $6\,\Omega$ resistors meet) be Node A at potential $V_A$.

Bottom branch: The positive terminal of the $2\text{ V}$ battery is at the reference, so its negative terminal (and hence the left end of the $3\,\Omega$ resistor) is at $-2\text{ V}$.
Top branch: The positive terminal of the $3\text{ V}$ battery is at the reference, so its negative terminal (and hence the node between the $6\,\Omega$ resistor and the $3\text{ V}$ battery) is at $-3\text{ V}$.

Applying KCL at Node A (sum of currents leaving the node is zero):
$\dfrac{V_A - 0}{4} + \dfrac{V_A - (-2)}{3} + \dfrac{V_A - (-3)}{6} = 0$

$\dfrac{V_A}{4} + \dfrac{V_A + 2}{3} + \dfrac{V_A + 3}{6} = 0$

Multiplying throughout by $12$:
$3V_A + 4(V_A + 2) + 2(V_A + 3) = 0$

$3V_A + 4V_A + 8 + 2V_A + 6 = 0$

$9V_A + 14 = 0 \Rightarrow V_A = -\dfrac{14}{9}\text{ V}$

Current through the $6\,\Omega$ resistor (from Node A towards the $-3\text{ V}$ point):
$I_6 = \dfrac{V_A - (-3)}{6} = \dfrac{-\dfrac{14}{9} + 3}{6} = \dfrac{\dfrac{13}{9}}{6} = \dfrac{13}{54}\text{ A}$

Heat generated in the $6\,\Omega$ resistor in $t = 100\text{ s}$:
$H = I_6^2 \cdot R \cdot t = \left(\dfrac{13}{54}\right)^2 \cdot 6 \cdot 100$

$H = \dfrac{169}{2916} \cdot 600 = \dfrac{169 \cdot 100}{486} = \dfrac{16900}{486}\text{ J}$

Given $H = \dfrac{\alpha}{100}\text{ J}$:
$\dfrac{\alpha}{100} = \dfrac{16900}{486}$

$\alpha = \dfrac{16900 \cdot 100}{486} = \dfrac{1690000}{486} \approx 3477.37$

Rounding to the nearest integer:
$\alpha = 3477$

Hence, the answer is $3477$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In an experiment to determine the resistance of a given wire using Ohm's law, the voltmeter and ammeter readings are noted as $10\text{ V}$ and $5\text{ A}$, respectively. The least counts of voltmeter and ammeter are $500\text{ mV}$ and $200\text{ mA}$, respectively. The estimated error in the resistance measurement is _______ $\Omega$.
questions.solution:
Given $V = 10\text{ V}$ and $I = 5\text{ A}$

Least count of voltmeter, $\Delta V = 500\text{ mV} = 0.5\text{ V}$

Least count of ammeter, $\Delta I = 200\text{ mA} = 0.2\text{ A}$

Resistance is given by Ohm's law:

$R = \dfrac{V}{I} = \dfrac{10}{5} = 2\text{ }\Omega$

The maximum permissible relative error in resistance is:

$\dfrac{\Delta R}{R} = \dfrac{\Delta V}{V} + \dfrac{\Delta I}{I}$

$\dfrac{\Delta R}{2} = \dfrac{0.5}{10} + \dfrac{0.2}{5}$

$\dfrac{\Delta R}{2} = 0.05 + 0.04 = 0.09$

$\Delta R = 2 \times 0.09 = 0.18\text{ }\Omega$

Answer: $0.18$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Under steady state condition the potential difference across the capacitor in the circuit is _______ V.
questions.solution:
In steady state, the capacitor acts as an open circuit, meaning no current flows through the middle branch.

The circuit simplifies to a single loop containing the $2 \text{ V}$ battery, the $6 \Omega$ resistor, and the $2 \Omega$ resistor.

The total resistance of this loop is $R_{\text{eq}} = 2 + 6 = 8 \Omega$.

The current flowing through the loop is $I = \dfrac{2}{8} = 0.25 \text{ A}$.

The potential difference across the parallel branches is equal to the voltage drop across the $2 \Omega$ resistor:
$V = I \times 2 = 0.25 \times 2 = 0.5 \text{ V}$

Since there is no current in the middle branch, the voltage drop across the $4 \Omega$ resistor is zero. Thus, the entire potential difference of $0.5 \text{ V}$ appears across the capacitor.

Answer: $0.5$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When an external resistance of $5\ \Omega$ is connected across terminals of a cell, a current of $0.25\text{ A}$ flows through it. When the $5\ \Omega$ resistor is replaced by a $2\ \Omega$ resistor, a current of $0.5\text{ A}$ flows through it. The internal resistance of the cell is _______ $\Omega$.
questions.solution:
Let the EMF of the cell be $E$ and its internal resistance be $r$.

The current $I$ in the circuit is given by $I = \dfrac{E}{R + r}$.

For the first case, $R_1 = 5\ \Omega$ and $I_1 = 0.25\text{ A}$:

$0.25 = \dfrac{E}{5 + r} \Rightarrow E = 0.25(5 + r)$

For the second case, $R_2 = 2\ \Omega$ and $I_2 = 0.5\text{ A}$:

$0.5 = \dfrac{E}{2 + r} \Rightarrow E = 0.5(2 + r)$

Equating the expressions for $E$:

$0.25(5 + r) = 0.5(2 + r)$

$5 + r = 2(2 + r)$

$5 + r = 4 + 2r$

$r = 1\ \Omega$

Answer: $1$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Refer to the figure given below. The values of $I_1$, $I_2$ and $I_3$ are __________.
questions.solution:
Using the principle of superposition, we analyse the circuit with one source active at a time.

Case 1: Only the $10\text{ V}$ source is active (the $5\text{ V}$ source is replaced by a short circuit).

With the $5\text{ V}$ source shorted, the top and bottom nodes of the bridge are directly connected by a wire, forming a Wheatstone bridge.

Checking for balance:
Left arm ratio: $\dfrac{4}{4} = 1$
Right arm ratio: $\dfrac{2}{2} = 1$

The ratios are equal, so the bridge is balanced. Hence, no current flows through the middle branch connecting the two nodes, and the contribution to $I_2$ from the $10\text{ V}$ source is $0\text{ A}$.

Equivalent resistance of the balanced bridge:
$(4 + 2)\,\Omega \parallel (4 + 2)\,\Omega = 6\,\Omega \parallel 6\,\Omega = 3\,\Omega$

Total resistance including the series $1\,\Omega$ resistor:
$R_{eq} = 3 + 1 = 4\,\Omega$

Current drawn from the $10\text{ V}$ source:
$I_{1(10V)} = \dfrac{10}{4} = 2.5\text{ A}$

This current splits equally between the two $6\,\Omega$ branches, so the current through the bottom $4\,\Omega$ resistor is:
$I_{3(10V)} = \dfrac{2.5}{2} = 1.25\text{ A}$

Case 2: Only the $5\text{ V}$ source is active (the $10\text{ V}$ source is replaced by a short circuit).

Now the $5\text{ V}$ source is applied across the top and bottom nodes, and the $1\,\Omega$ resistor lies in the middle branch between the left and centre nodes.

For the left branch ($4\,\Omega$ and $4\,\Omega$ in series), the potential at the midpoint is $\dfrac{5}{2} = 2.5\text{ V}$.
For the right branch ($2\,\Omega$ and $2\,\Omega$ in series), the potential at the midpoint is also $\dfrac{5}{2} = 2.5\text{ V}$.

Since both midpoints are at the same potential, no current flows through the $1\,\Omega$ middle branch. Hence, the contribution to $I_1$ from the $5\text{ V}$ source is $0\text{ A}$.

Equivalent resistance seen by the $5\text{ V}$ source:
$(4 + 4)\,\Omega \parallel (2 + 2)\,\Omega = 8\,\Omega \parallel 4\,\Omega = \dfrac{8 \times 4}{8 + 4} = \dfrac{8}{3}\,\Omega$

Total current supplied by the $5\text{ V}$ source:
$I_{2(5V)} = \dfrac{5}{8/3} = \dfrac{15}{8} = 1.875\text{ A}$

Current through the left branch (which includes the bottom $4\,\Omega$ resistor):
$I_{3(5V)} = \dfrac{5}{8} = 0.625\text{ A}$

Applying superposition:
$I_1 = I_{1(10V)} + I_{1(5V)} = 2.5 + 0 = 2.5\text{ A}$
$I_2 = I_{2(10V)} + I_{2(5V)} = 0 + 1.875 = 1.875\text{ A}$
$I_3 = I_{3(10V)} + I_{3(5V)} = 1.25 + 0.625 = 1.875\text{ A}$

Hence, the correct option is $(1)\ I_1 = 2.5\text{ A},\ I_2 = 1.875\text{ A},\ I_3 = 1.875\text{ A}$.

The ratios are equal, so the bridge is balanced. Hence, no current flows through the middle branch connecting the two nodes, and the contribution to $I_2$ from the $10\text{ V}$ source is $0\text{ A}$.

Equivalent resistance of the balanced bridge:
$(4 + 2)\,\Omega \parallel (4 + 2)\,\Omega = 6\,\Omega \parallel 6\,\Omega = 3\,\Omega$

Total resistance including the series $1\,\Omega$ resistor:
$R_{eq} = 3 + 1 = 4\,\Omega$

Current drawn from the $10\text{ V}$ source:
$I_{1(10V)} = \dfrac{10}{4} = 2.5\text{ A}$

This current splits equally between the two $6\,\Omega$ branches, so the current through the bottom $4\,\Omega$ resistor is:
$I_{3(10V)} = \dfrac{2.5}{2} = 1.25\text{ A}$

Case 2: Only the $5\text{ V}$ source is active (the $10\text{ V}$ source is replaced by a short circuit).

Now the $5\text{ V}$ source is applied across the top and bottom nodes, and the $1\,\Omega$ resistor lies in the middle branch between the left and centre nodes.

For the left branch ($4\,\Omega$ and $4\,\Omega$ in series), the potential at the midpoint is $\dfrac{5}{2} = 2.5\text{ V}$.
For the right branch ($2\,\Omega$ and $2\,\Omega$ in series), the potential at the midpoint is also $\dfrac{5}{2} = 2.5\text{ V}$.

Since both midpoints are at the same potential, no current flows through the $1\,\Omega$ middle branch. Hence, the contribution to $I_1$ from the $5\text{ V}$ source is $0\text{ A}$.

Equivalent resistance seen by the $5\text{ V}$ source:
$(4 + 4)\,\Omega \parallel (2 + 2)\,\Omega = 8\,\Omega \parallel 4\,\Omega = \dfrac{8 \times 4}{8 + 4} = \dfrac{8}{3}\,\Omega$

Total current supplied by the $5\text{ V}$ source:
$I_{2(5V)} = \dfrac{5}{8/3} = \dfrac{15}{8} = 1.875\text{ A}$

Current through the left branch (which includes the bottom $4\,\Omega$ resistor):
$I_{3(5V)} = \dfrac{5}{8} = 0.625\text{ A}$

Applying superposition:
$I_1 = I_{1(10V)} + I_{1(5V)} = 2.5 + 0 = 2.5\text{ A}$
$I_2 = I_{2(10V)} + I_{2(5V)} = 0 + 1.875 = 1.875\text{ A}$
$I_3 = I_{3(10V)} + I_{3(5V)} = 1.25 + 0.625 = 1.875\text{ A}$

Hence, the correct option is $(1)\ I_1 = 2.5\text{ A},\ I_2 = 1.875\text{ A},\ I_3 = 1.875\text{ A}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Refer to the figure given below, current between terminals $A$ and $B$ is _____ A.
questions.solution:
The given circuit consists of four parallel branches connected between the left and right common vertical wires.

Let's find the equivalent electromotive force (EMF) and resistance for each branch:
For the top three active branches, each contains three $5\text{ V}$ cells and three $3\ \Omega$ resistors in series.
Equivalent EMF of each active branch, $E = 5 + 5 + 5 = 15\text{ V}$.
Equivalent resistance of each active branch, $R = 3 + 3 + 3 = 9\ \Omega$.

Since these three identical active branches are connected in parallel, we can replace them with a single equivalent voltage source:
Equivalent EMF, $E_{eq} = 15\text{ V}$ (as they are identical and in parallel).
Equivalent internal resistance, $R_{eq} = \dfrac{9}{3} = 3\ \Omega$.

The fourth (bottom) branch is connected between terminals $A$ and $B$ and acts as the load for this equivalent source. It contains three $3\ \Omega$ resistors in series.
Resistance of the branch $AB$, $R_{AB} = 3 + 3 + 3 = 9\ \Omega$.

Now, the circuit is simplified to an equivalent source of $15\text{ V}$ with internal resistance $3\ \Omega$ connected across a load of $9\ \Omega$.
The current $I$ flowing between terminals $A$ and $B$ (through the bottom branch) is given by Ohm's law:
$I = \dfrac{E_{eq}}{R_{eq} + R_{AB}}$

$I = \dfrac{15}{3 + 9} = \dfrac{15}{12}\text{ A}$

$I = 1.25\text{ A}$

Answer: $1.25$

questions.q: A voltmeter with internal resistance of $x\ \Omega$ can be used to measure upto $20$ V. In order to increase its measuring range to $30$ V, the required modification is to _____.
options: connect resistor of $\dfrac{x}{2}\ \Omega$, in series with voltmeter.
connect resistor of $\dfrac{x}{2}\ \Omega$, in parallel to voltmeter.
connect a resistor of $x\ \Omega$ in series with voltmeter.
connect resistor of $2x\ \Omega$ in parallel to voltmeter.
questions.solution:
Let the maximum current for full-scale deflection of the voltmeter be $I_g$.

$I_g = \dfrac{V_1}{R_v} = \dfrac{20}{x}$

To increase the measuring range to $V_2 = 30$ V, a resistance $R$ must be connected in series with the voltmeter.

$V_2 = I_g(R_v + R)$

$30 = \dfrac{20}{x}(x + R)$

$30x = 20x + 20R$

$10x = 20R$

$R = \dfrac{x}{2}\ \Omega$

Thus, a resistor of $\dfrac{x}{2}\ \Omega$ should be connected in series with the voltmeter.

Answer: connect resistor of $\dfrac{x}{2}\ \Omega$, in series with voltmeter.

The four parallel branches between the common left node $A$ and the common right node are all identical: each consists of a $27\text{ V}$ source in series with a $3\ \Omega$ resistor. Thevenin equivalent between $A$ and $B$:
Since all four branches have the same EMF and polarity in parallel:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two resistors of $200 \, \Omega$ and $400 \, \Omega$ are connected in series with a battery of $100$ V. A bulb rated at $200$ V, $100$ W is connected across the $400 \, \Omega$ resistance. The potential drop across the bulb is _______ V.
questions.solution:
The resistance of the bulb is calculated using its power rating:

$R_b = \dfrac{V^2}{P} = \dfrac{200^2}{100} = 400 \, \Omega$

The bulb is connected in parallel with the $400 \, \Omega$ resistor. The equivalent resistance of this parallel combination is:

$R_p = \dfrac{400 \times 400}{400 + 400} = 200 \, \Omega$

This parallel combination is in series with the $200 \, \Omega$ resistor. The total equivalent resistance of the circuit is:

$R_{eq} = 200 + R_p = 200 + 200 = 400 \, \Omega$

The current drawn from the battery is:

$I = \dfrac{V}{R_{eq}} = \dfrac{100}{400} = 0.25 \text{ A}$

The potential drop across the bulb is the same as the potential drop across the parallel combination:

$V_p = I \times R_p = 0.25 \times 200 = 50 \text{ V}$

Answer: $50$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which one of the following is not a measurable quantity?
questions.solution:
In electrostatics and circuit theory, potential (voltage) at a single point is defined relative to a reference point (usually infinity or ground where potential is assumed to be zero).
Absolute voltage at a point is not a physically measurable quantity because only the difference in potential between two points can be measured using instruments like a voltmeter.
Resistance can be measured using an ohmmeter or bridge circuits.
Displacement current is a physical quantity that can be calculated and its effects (magnetic field) can be measured.
Voltage difference (potential difference) is the standard quantity measured between two points in a circuit.
Therefore, absolute voltage is not a measurable quantity.

questions.q: A Wheatstone bridge is initially at room temperature and all arms of the bridge have same value of resistances $\left(R_{1}=R_{2}=R_{3}=R_{4}\right)$. When $R_{3}$ resistance is heated to some temperature, its resistance value has gone up by $10 \%$. The potential difference $\left(V_{a}-V_{b}\right)$ (after $R_{3}$ is heated) is $\_\_\_\_$ V.
questions.solution:
Initially, the Wheatstone bridge is balanced with $R_1 = R_2 = R_3 = R_4 = R$.
Since the bridge is balanced, the potential difference across the bridge is zero: $V_a - V_b = 0$ V.
When $R_3$ is heated and its resistance increases by 10%: $R_3' = 1.1R$
The voltage at node $a$ (between $R_1$ and $R_2$): $V_a = 40 \times \frac{R_2}{R_1 + R_2} = 40 \times \frac{R}{R + R} = 40 \times \frac{1}{2} = 20$ V
The voltage at node $b$ (between $R_3'$ and $R_4$): $V_b = 40 \times \frac{R_4}{R_3' + R_4} = 40 \times \frac{R}{1.1R + R} = 40 \times \frac{1}{2.1} \approx 19.05$ V
Therefore: $V_a - V_b = 20 - 19.05 = 0.95$ V

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: For the two cells having same EMF $E$ and internal resistance $r$, the current passing through the external resistor $6 \Omega$ is same when both the cells are connected either in parallel or in series. The value of internal resistance $r$ is $\_\_\_\_$\Omega$.
questions.solution:
For series connection of two cells: $I_s = \frac{2E}{2r + 6}$.
For parallel connection: $I_p = \frac{E}{r/2 + 6} = \frac{2E}{r + 12}$.
Given $I_s = I_p$: $\frac{2E}{2r + 6} = \frac{2E}{r + 12}$.
This gives $2r + 6 = r + 12$, so $r = 6\Omega$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In the potentiometer, when the cell in the secondary circuit is shunted with $4 \Omega$ resistance, the balance is obtained at the length 120 cm of wire. Now when the same cell is shunted with $12 \Omega$ resistance, the balance is shifted to a length of 180 cm. The internal resistance of cell is $\_\_\_\_$\Omega$
questions.solution:
In a potentiometer, the internal resistance $r$ of a cell is given by the formula $r = R \left( \frac{l_0}{l} - 1 \right)$, where $l_0$ is the balancing length in open circuit, $l$ is the balancing length when shunted with resistance $R$.
This can be rewritten as $\frac{l_0}{l} = 1 + \frac{r}{R}$ or $l = \frac{l_0}{1 + r/R}$.
Case 1: $R_1 = 4 \Omega$ and $l_1 = 120$ cm.
$120 = \frac{l_0}{1 + r/4} = \frac{4l_0}{4 + r}$ ... (i)
Case 2: $R_2 = 12 \Omega$ and $l_2 = 180$ cm.
$180 = \frac{l_0}{1 + r/12} = \frac{12l_0}{12 + r}$ ... (ii)
Dividing equation (ii) by (i):
$\frac{180}{120} = \frac{12l_0}{12 + r} \times \frac{4 + r}{4l_0}$
$\frac{3}{2} = \frac{3(4 + r)}{12 + r}$
$\frac{1}{2} = \frac{4 + r}{12 + r}$
$12 + r = 8 + 2r$
$r = 4 \Omega$
The internal resistance of the cell is $4 \Omega$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The equivalent resistance between the points $A$ and $B$ in the following circuit is $\frac{x}{5} \Omega$. The value of $x$ is $\_\_\_\_$.
questions.solution:
Using Kirchhoff's laws on the bridge circuit with resistances $6\Omega, 3\Omega, 3\Omega, 3\Omega, 6\Omega$ and applying a 1V test voltage:

From the loop equation:
$6i_1 + 3(2i_1 - i) = 3(i - i_1)$

$15i_1 = 6i \Rightarrow i_1 = \frac{2}{5}i$ ...(1)

From the second loop:
$3(i - i_1) + 6i_1 = 1$
$3i + 3i_1 = 1$

$\left(3 + \frac{6}{5}\right)i = 1$

$i = \frac{5}{21} A = \frac{1V}{R_{eq}}$

$R_{eq} = \frac{21}{5} = 4.2 \ \Omega$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A moving coil galvanometer of resistance $100 \Omega$ shows a full scale deflection for a current of 1 mA. The value of resistance required to convert this galvanometer into an ammeter, showing full scale deflection for a current of 5 mA, is $\_\_\_\_$\Omega$
questions.solution:
To convert a galvanometer to an ammeter, a shunt resistance $S$ is connected in parallel. For full-scale deflection:
Current through galvanometer: $I_g = 1$ mA
Total current: $I = 5$ mA
Current through shunt: $I_s = 5 - 1 = 4$ mA
Since voltage across both is equal: $I_g \cdot G = I_s \cdot S$
$0.001 \times 100 = 0.004 \times S$
$S = \frac{0.1}{0.004} = 25$ Ω

questions.q: In a meter bridge experiment to determine the value of unknown resistance, first the resistances $2 \Omega$ and $3 \Omega$ are connected in the left and right gaps of the bridge and the null point is obtained at a distance $l \mathrm{~cm}$ from the left. Now when an unknown resistance $x \Omega$ is connected in parallel to $3 \Omega$ resistance, the null point is shifted by 10 cm to the right of wire. The value of unknown resistance $x$ is $\_\_\_\_$\Omega$.
questions.solution:
Meter bridge null point condition: $\frac{R_1}{R_2} = \frac{l}{100-l}$
Initial: $R_1 = 2Ω$, $R_2 = 3Ω$, null at $l$ cm
$\frac{2}{3} = \frac{l}{100-l}$ gives $2(100-l) = 3l$, so $l = 40$ cm
When $xΩ$ connected in parallel with $3Ω$: $R_2' = \frac{3x}{3+x}Ω$
New null point at $(40+10) = 50$ cm from left:
$\frac{2}{R_2'} = \frac{50}{50} = 1$
$\frac{2(3+x)}{3x} = 1$ gives $6 + 2x = 3x$
$x = 6Ω$
questions.question: In a meter bridge experiment to determine the value of unknown resistance, first the resistances $2 \Omega$ and $3 \Omega$ are connected in the left and right gaps of the bridge and the null point is obtained at a distance $l \mathrm{~cm}$ from the left. Now when an unknown resistance $x \Omega$ is connected in parallel to $3 \Omega$ resistance, the null point is shifted by 10 cm to the right of wire. The value of unknown resistance $x$ is $\_\_\_\_$\Omega$.
questions.explanation:
Meter bridge null point condition: $\frac{R_1}{R_2} = \frac{l}{100-l}$
Initial: $R_1 = 2Ω$, $R_2 = 3Ω$, null at $l$ cm
$\frac{2}{3} = \frac{l}{100-l}$ gives $2(100-l) = 3l$, so $l = 40$ cm
When $xΩ$ connected in parallel with $3Ω$: $R_2' = \frac{3x}{3+x}Ω$
New null point at $(40+10) = 50$ cm from left:
$\frac{2}{R_2'} = \frac{50}{50} = 1$
$\frac{2(3+x)}{3x} = 1$ gives $6 + 2x = 3x$
$x = 6Ω$

questions.q: Two resistors $2 \Omega$ and $3 \Omega$ are connected in the gaps of bridge as shown in figure. The null point is obtained with the contact of jockey at some point on wire $X Y$. When an unknown resistor is connected in parallel with $3 \Omega$ resistor, the null point is shifted by 22.5 cm toward $Y$. The resistance of unknown resistor is $\_\_\_\_$\Omega$.
questions.solution:
In a Wheatstone bridge with 2Ω and 3Ω, the null point is found when $\frac{R_1}{R_2} = \frac{l}{L-l}$.
Initial balance: $\frac{2}{3} = \frac{l_1}{L-l_1}$ gives $l_1 = \frac{2L}{5}$.
For standard wire length $L = 100$ cm, $l_1 = 40$ cm.
When unknown resistance $R$ is connected in parallel with 3Ω, equivalent resistance becomes $\frac{3R}{3+R}$.
New null point: $\frac{2}{\frac{3R}{3+R}} = \frac{l_2}{L-l_2}$, which simplifies to $\frac{2(3+R)}{3R} = \frac{l_2}{L-l_2}$.
Null point shifts 22.5 cm toward Y: $l_2 = 40 + 22.5 = 62.5$ cm.
Substituting: $\frac{2(3+R)}{3R} = \frac{62.5}{37.5} = \frac{5}{3}$
$6(3+R) = 15R \Rightarrow 18 = 9R \Rightarrow R = 2$ Ω

questions.q: Two resistors of $100 \Omega$ each are connected in series with a 9 V battery. A voltmeter of $400 \Omega$ resistance is connected to measure the voltage drop across one of the resistors. The voltmeter reading is $\_\_\_\_$ V.
questions.solution:
When the 400Ω voltmeter is connected in parallel with one 100Ω resistor, the equivalent resistance is
$R_{eq} = \frac{100 \times 400}{500} = 80Ω$.
Total circuit resistance: $R_{total} = 100 + 80 = 180Ω$.
Circuit current: $I = 9/180 = 0.05$ A.
Voltmeter reading (voltage across parallel combination): $V = 0.05 \times 80 = 4$ V

questions.q: To compare EMF of two cells using potentiometer the balancing lengths obtained are 200 cm and 150 cm. The least count of scale is 1 cm. The percentage error in the ratio of EMFs is $\_\_\_\_$.
questions.solution:
$\epsilon = \lambda \ell$ (Potential gradient)

$\epsilon_1 = \lambda \ell_1$
$\epsilon_2 = \lambda \ell_2$

$y = \frac{\epsilon_1}{\epsilon_2} = \frac{\ell_1}{\ell_2}$

$\frac{\Delta y}{y} = \frac{\Delta \ell_1}{\ell_1} + \frac{\Delta \ell_2}{\ell_2}$

$\frac{\Delta y}{y} = \frac{1}{200} + \frac{1}{150}$

$\frac{\Delta y}{y} \times 100 = \left(\frac{1}{200} + \frac{1}{150}\right) \times 100 = \left(\frac{3+4}{600}\right) \times 100 = \frac{7}{6} = 1.16\%$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A wire of uniform resistance $\lambda \Omega / \mathrm{m}$ is bent into a circle of radius $r$ and another piece of wire with length $2 r$ is connected between points $A$ and $B(A O B)$ as shown in figure. The equivalent resistance between points $A$ and $B$ is $\_\_\_\_$\Omega$.
questions.solution:
The wire bent into a circle of radius $r$ has resistance $\lambda \cdot \pi r$ for the semicircular arcs, and the straight wire of length $2r$ has resistance $\lambda \cdot 2r$. The three paths between A and B (two semicircular arcs of the circle and one straight wire through center) are in parallel.

$\frac{1}{R_{AB}} = \frac{2}{\lambda \pi r} + \frac{1}{\lambda \cdot 2r} + \frac{2}{\lambda \cdot 3\pi r}$

$= \frac{1}{\lambda r} \left[\frac{2}{\pi} + \frac{1}{2} + \frac{2}{3\pi}\right]$

$= \frac{1}{\lambda r} \left(\frac{12 + 3\pi + 4}{6\pi}\right) = \frac{1}{\lambda r} \cdot \frac{16 + 3\pi}{6\pi}$

$R_{AB} = \lambda r \left(\frac{6\pi}{16 + 3\pi}\right) = \frac{6\pi \lambda r}{3\pi + 16}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An electric power line having total resistance of $2 \Omega$, delivers 1 kW of power at 250 V. The percentage efficiency of transmission line is $\_\_\_\_$ .
questions.solution:
Current in transmission line: $I = \frac{P}{V} = \frac{1000}{250} = 4$ A.
Power loss: $P_{loss} = I^2 R = 4^2 \times 2 = 32$ W.
Efficiency: $\eta = \frac{P - P_{loss}}{P} \times 100\%$
$= \frac{1000 - 32}{1000} \times 100\%$
$= 96.8\%$ which rounds to 96.9%.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A cylindrical conductor of length 2 m and area of cross-section $0.2 \mathrm{~mm}^{2}$ carries an electric current of 1.6 A when its ends are connected to a 2 V battery. Mobility of electrons in the conductor is $\alpha \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~m}^{2} / V. s$. The value of $\alpha$ is :
(electron concentration $=5 \times 10^{28} / \mathrm{m}^{3}$ and electron charge $\left.=1.6 \times 10^{-19} \mathrm{C}\right)$
questions.solution:
For a cylindrical conductor with length 2 m, cross-section 0.2 mm² = 0.2 × 10⁻⁶ m², carrying 1.6 A at 2 V.
Resistance: $R = V/I = 2/1.6 = 1.25$ Ω.
Resistivity: $\rho = RA/L = 1.25 \times 0.2 \times 10^{-6}/2$
$= 0.125 \times 10^{-6}$ Ω·m.
Using $\rho = 1/(ne\mu)$, mobility: $\mu = 1/(ne\rho)$
$= 1/(5 \times 10^{28} \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \times 0.125 \times 10^{-6})$
$= 1/(1 \times 10^3) = 10^{-3}$ m²/V·s.
Thus $\alpha = 1$.

questions.q: A meter bridge with two resistances $R_{1}$ and $R_{2}$ as shown in figure was balanced (null point) at 40 cm from the point $P$. The null point changed to 50 cm from the point $P$, when $16 \Omega$ resistance is connected in parallel to $R_{2}$. The values of resistances $R_{1}$ and $R_{2}$ are $\_\_\_\_$.
questions.solution:
Initial balance at 40 cm: $\frac{R_1}{R_2} = \frac{40}{60} = \frac{2}{3}$ ...(i)
With $16\,\Omega$ parallel to $R_2$, null point at 50 cm:
$\frac{R_1}{\frac{16R_2}{16+R_2}} = \frac{50}{50} = 1 \Rightarrow R_1 = \frac{16R_2}{16+R_2}$ ...(ii)
From (i): $R_1 = \frac{2}{3}R_2$.
Substituting in (ii): $\frac{2}{3}R_2 = \frac{16R_2}{16+R_2}$.
$\frac{2}{3} = \frac{16}{16+R_2} \Rightarrow 2(16+R_2) = 48 \Rightarrow R_2 = 8\,\Omega$.
$R_1 = \frac{16}{3}\,\Omega$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two known resistances of $R \Omega$ and $2 R \Omega$ and one unknown resistance $X \Omega$ are connected in a circuit as shown in the figure. If the equivalent resistance between points $A$ and $B$ in the circuit is $X \Omega$, then the value of $X$ is $\_\_\_\_$\Omega$.
questions.solution:
The circuit has 2R and X in series (top branch) parallel to R (bottom branch).
The equivalent resistance is $R_{eq} = \frac{(2R + X) \cdot R}{3R + X} = X$.
Setting up the equation: $X(3R + X) = R(2R + X)$, which simplifies to $X^2 + 2RX - 2R^2 = 0$.
Using the quadratic formula: $X = \frac{-2R \pm 2R\sqrt{3}}{2} = R(-1 \pm \sqrt{3})$.
Since resistance must be positive, $X = (\sqrt{3} - 1)R$ Ω.

questions.q: The total length of potentiometer wire AB is 50 cm in the arrangement as shown in figure. If $P$ is the point where the galvanometer shows zero reading then the length $A P$ is $\_\_\_\_$ cm.
questions.solution:
In this potentiometer, for zero galvanometer reading, the potential at P must equal the potential at the junction between the 6Ω and 4Ω resistors.
The voltage distribution across the resistors is $V_{junction} = E \times \frac{6}{6+4} = 0.6E$ from point A.
Since the potentiometer wire is uniform with length 50 cm, the potential distribution is also uniform.
Therefore, $\frac{AP}{AB} = \frac{6}{10}$, giving $AP = 50 \times 0.6 = 30$ cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A battery with EMF $E$ and internal resistance $r$ is connected across a resistance $R$. The power consumption in $R$ will be maximum when :
questions.solution:
Power consumed in external resistance R is $P = \frac{E^2 R}{(R + r)^2}$.
To find maximum, differentiate with respect to R:
$\frac{dP}{dR} = E^2 \frac{(R + r)^2 - 2R(R + r)}{(R + r)^4} = E^2 \frac{r - R}{(R + r)^3}$.
$\frac{dP}{dR} = 0$ gives $R = r$.
This is the maximum power transfer theorem: maximum power is delivered when the external load resistance equals the source internal resistance.

questions.q: Two cells of emf 1 V and 2 V and internal resistance $2 \Omega$ and $1 \Omega$, respectively, are connected in series with an external resistance of $6 \Omega$. The total current in the circuit is $\mathrm{I}_1$. Now the same two cells in parallel configuration are connected to same external resistance. In this case, the total current drawn is $I_2$. The value of $\left(\frac{I_1}{I_2}\right)$ is $\frac{x}{3}$. The value of $x$ is _____.
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \varepsilon_{\mathrm{eq}}=3 \\ & \mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{eq}}=9 \\ & \mathrm{i}_1=\frac{3}{9}=\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned} \varepsilon_{\mathrm{eq}}=\frac{\frac{\varepsilon_1}{\mathrm{r}_1}+\frac{\varepsilon_2}{\mathrm{r}_2}}{\frac{1}{\mathrm{r}_1}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{r}_2}} \varepsilon_{\mathrm{eq}}=\frac{\frac{1}{2}+\frac{2}{1}}{\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{1}}=\frac{5}{3} \begin{aligned} & \mathrm{r}_{\text{equ }}=\frac{2 \times 1}{3}+6=\frac{20}{3} \\ & \mathrm{i}_2=\frac{1}{4} \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{i}_1}{\mathrm{i}_2}=\frac{4}{3}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: In the figure shown below, a resistance of $150.4 \Omega$ is connected in series to an ammeter A of resistance $240 \Omega$. A shunt resistance of $10 \Omega$ is connected in parallel with the ammeter. The reading of the ammeter is _____ mA.
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{eq}}=\mathrm{R}_1+\mathrm{R}_2 \\ & \mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{eq}}=150.4+\frac{240 \times 10}{250} \\ & =150.4+9.6=160 \Omega \\ & \mathrm{I}_1=\frac{\mathrm{I} \mathrm{R}_2}{240} \\ & \mathrm{I}_1=\frac{\mathrm{I} \times 9.6}{240} \\ & =\frac{20}{160} \times \frac{9.6}{2400}=\frac{1}{200}=5 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~A}=5 \mathrm{~mA}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The battery of a mobile phone is rated as 4.2 V , 5800 mAh. How much energy is stored in it when fully charged ?
questions.solution:
Given $\mathrm{V}=4.2$ volt
$\therefore$ Energy supplied by battery
$=\mathrm{vq}=4.2 \times 5800 \times 3600 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~J}=87.696 \mathrm{~kJ}$
$\therefore$ Energy stored in the battery when fully charged
$=87.696 \mathrm{~kJ} \approx 87.7 \mathrm{~kJ}$

questions.q:
A wire of resistance R is bent into an equilateral triangle and an identical wire is bent into $a$ square. The ratio of resistance between the two end points of an edge of the triangle to that of the square is
Options
questions.solution:
For the wire bent into an equilateral triangle, each side has a resistance $\frac{R}{3}$.

$R_{\text{eq }}=\frac{\left(\frac{2 R}{3}\right)\left(\frac{R}{3}\right)}{\frac{2 R}{3}+\frac{R}{3}}=\frac{2 R}{9}=R_1$ (lets say)
For the wire bent into a square, each side has a resistance $\frac{R}{4}$.

$\begin{aligned} & R_{\text{eq }}=\frac{\left(\frac{3 R}{4}\right)\left(\frac{R}{4}\right)}{\frac{3 R}{4}+\frac{R}{4}}=\frac{3 R}{16}=R_3 \text{ (lets say) } \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{R_1}{R_3}=\frac{\frac{2 R}{9}}{\frac{3 R}{16}}=\frac{32}{27}\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements :
Statement-I : The equivalent emf of two nonideal batteries connected in parallel is smaller than either of the two emfs.
Statement-II : The equivalent internal resistance of two nonideal batteries connected in parallel is smaller than the internal resistance of either of the two batteries.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are false
Statement-I is false but Statement-II is true
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are true
Statement-I is true but Statement-II is false
questions.solution:
In parallel connections
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{1}{r_{\mathrm{eq}}}=\frac{1}{r_1}+\frac{1}{r_2} \\
& \frac{E_{\mathrm{eq}}}{r_{\mathrm{eq}}}=\frac{E_1}{r_1}+\frac{E_2}{r_2}
\end{aligned}$
If E_1=E_2 and $r_1=r_2, E_{\text{eq }}=E_1=E_2 \therefore$ Statement 1 is false.
$r_{\text{eq }}$ is less then both r_1 and $r_2 \therefore$ Statement II is true

questions.q: A wire of resistance $R$ and radius $r$ is stretched till its radius became $r / 2$. If new resistance of the stretched wire is $x R$, then value of $x$ is _______
questions.solution:
We know $\mathrm{R}=\frac{\rho l}{\mathrm{ A}}, \mathrm{R} \propto \frac{l}{\mathrm{r}^2}$
As we starch the wire, its length will increase but its radius will decrease keeping the volume constant
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{i}}=\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{f}} \\
& \pi \mathrm{r}^2 l=\pi \frac{\mathrm{r}^2}{4} l_{\mathrm{f}} \\
& l_{\mathrm{f}}=4 l \\
& \frac{\mathrm{R}_{\text{new }}}{\mathrm{R}_{\text{old }}}=\left(\frac{4 l}{\frac{\mathrm{r}^2}{4}}\right) \frac{\mathrm{r}^2}{l}=16 \\
& \mathrm{R}_{\text{new }}=16 \mathrm{R} \\
\therefore & \mathrm{x}=16
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: In a metre-bridge when a resistance in the left gap is $2Ω$ and unknown resistance in the right gap, the balance length is found to be $40cm .$ On shunting the unknown resistance with $2Ω,$ the balance length changes by:
questions.solution:
In first circuit:

For balanced condition, we get $\dfrac{2}{40} = \dfrac{X}{60} ⇒ X = 3Ω$

In second case:

Net resistance of the right side due to shunting becomes,  ${X}^{'} = \dfrac{2 \times 3}{2 + 3} = 1 . 2Ω$

Again for balanced condition, 

$\dfrac{2}{ℓ} = \dfrac{1 . 2}{100 - ℓ}$

$⇒ 200 - 2ℓ = 1 . 2ℓ$

$⇒ ℓ = \dfrac{200}{3 . 2} = 62 . 5cm$

Clearly, balance length changes by $22 . 5cm$.

questions.q: In an ammeter, $5 %$ of the main current passes through the galvanometer. If resistance of the galvanometer is $G,$ the resistance of ammeter will be:
questions.solution:
As potential drop across both branches would be the same, we get ${I}_{S}S = {I}_{g}G$

$\left(\dfrac{95}{100}I\right)S = \left(\dfrac{5I}{100}\right)G$

$⇒ S = \dfrac{G}{19}$

Now, resistance of ammeter will be

${R}_{A} = \dfrac{SG}{S + G} = \dfrac{\dfrac{{G}^{2}}{19}}{\dfrac{20G}{19}}$

$⇒ {R}_{A} = \dfrac{G}{20}$

For no deflection(balanced condition) $\dfrac{0 . 8}{1} = \dfrac{R}{3}$

$= - 1 \times {10}^{- 2} ° {C}^{- 1}$

Power through the resistor is given by, $P = {I}^{2}R$.

questions.q: In the following circuit, the battery has an emf of $2V$ and an internal resistance of $\dfrac{2}{3}Ω$. The power consumption in the entire circuit is ______ $W$.
questions.solution:
As we can see, two resistances of $2Ω$ in the middle portion(in both left and right side) are in parallel, so their combined resistance will be $\dfrac{2 \times 2}{2 + 2} + \dfrac{2 \times 2}{2 + 2} = 2Ω$. Now this resistance along with the topmost & bottommost resistance are in parallel again, so total resistance of the circuit will be,

${R}_{eq} = \dfrac{2}{3} + \dfrac{2}{3} = \dfrac{4}{3}Ω$

$∴ P = \dfrac{{V}^{2}}{{R}_{eq}} = \dfrac{4}{\dfrac{4}{3}} = 3W$

Resistance at $27 ° C$, ${R}_{T = 27} = 60Ω$.

Given that
Current $I = {I}_{0} + \betat$, ${I}_{0} = 20A$ and $\beta = 3A{s}^{- 1}$

The instantaneous current is given by

$I = 20 + 3t . . . \left(1\right)$

Integrating equation (1), we have

$\dfrac{dq}{dt} = 20 + 3t ⇒ {∫}_{0}^{q}dq = {∫}_{0}^{20} ( 20 + 3t ) dt ⇒ q = {∫}_{0}^{20}20dt + {∫}_{0}^{20}3tdt ⇒ q = {\left[20t + \dfrac{3{t}^{2}}{2}\right]}_{0}^{20} = 1000C$

questions.q: Wheatstone bridge principle is used to measure the specific resistance $\left({S}_{1}\right)$ of given wire, having length $L$, radius $r$. If $X$ is the resistance of wire, then specific resistance is : ${S}_{1} = X \left(\dfrac{\pi{r}^{2}}{L}\right). If the length of the wire gets doubled then the value of specific resistance will be :$
questions.solution:
The specific resistance of a material, also known as electrical resistivity, is a measure of how strongly a specific material opposes the flow of electric current.

Specific resistance is an intrinsic property of a material and is dependent on factors such as the material's composition, temperature, and crystal structure. It is the counterpart of conductivity, with which it is inversely proportional.

Hence, even if the length of the wire is doubled, the specific resistance remains the same, i.e., ${S}_{1}$.

questions.q: A wire of resistance $R$ and length $L$ is cut into $5$ equal parts. If these parts are joined parallely, then resultant resistance will be :
questions.solution:
Resistance of each part will be equally divided. So, the resistance of each part of the wire can be expressed as $\dfrac{R}{5}$.

The formula to calculate the equivalent resistance of the combination of resistors is given by

$\dfrac{1}{{R}_{eq}} = \mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{5}\dfrac{1}{{R}_{i}} . . . \left(1\right)$

From equation (1), it follows that

$\dfrac{1}{{R}_{eq}} = \dfrac{5}{R} + \dfrac{5}{R} + \dfrac{5}{R} + \dfrac{5}{R} + \dfrac{5}{R} = \dfrac{25}{R} ⇒ {R}_{eq} = \dfrac{R}{25}$

questions.q: A wire of length $10cm$ and radius $\sqrt{7} \times {10}^{- 4}m$ connected across the right gap of a meter bridge. When a resistance of $4 . 5Ω$ is connected on the left gap by using a resistance box, the balance length is found to be at $60cm$ from the left end. If the resistivity of the wire is $R \times {10}^{- 7}Ωm$, then value of $R$ is :
questions.solution:
From the null point condition of a Meter Bridge, it follows that,

$\dfrac{4 . 5Ω}{60} = \dfrac{X}{100 - 60} ⇒ X = \dfrac{40}{60} \times 4 . 5Ω = 3Ω$

Also,

$\begin{cases}X & = & \dfrac{ρl}{A} \\ & = & \dfrac{ρl}{\pi{r}^{2}} . . . \left(1\right)\end{cases}$

From equation (1), it follows that

$3 = ρ \times \dfrac{0 . 1}{\pi \times {\left(\sqrt{7} \times {10}^{- 4}\right)}^{2}} ⇒ ρ = \dfrac{3 \times \pi \times {\left(\sqrt{7} \times {10}^{- 4}\right)}^{2}}{0 . 1} \approx 66 \times {10}^{- 7}Ωm$

Therefore, $R = 66$.

Given below are two statements:

Statement I : The equivalent resistance of resistors in a series combination is smaller than least resistance used in the combination.

Statement II : The resistivity of the material is independent of temperature. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement $I$ and Statement $II$ are false
Both Statement $I$ and Statement $II$ are true
Statement $I$ is true but Statement $II$ is false
Statement $I$ is false but Statement $II$ is true
questions.solution:
The formula for series equivalent resistance is given by

${R}_{s} = {R}_{1} + {R}_{2} + . . . . . . + {R}_{n}$.

Hence, the equivalent resistance will be the highest value compared to other resistances.

The resistivity of a material is given by,

$ρ = {ρ}^{0}\left(1 + \alpha\DeltaT\right)$

Clearly, the resistivity is dependant on temperature.

Hence, this is the right option.

questions.q: A network of four resistances is connected to $9V$ battery, as shown in figure. The magnitude of voltage difference between the points $A$ and $B$ is __________ $V$.
questions.solution:
The resistance in each branch is $6Ω$. They are in parallel. So, net resistance is $R ' = \dfrac{6}{2} = 3Ω$.

The total current flowing through the loop,

$I = \dfrac{V}{R '} = \dfrac{9V}{3Ω} = 3A$

Thus, through each branch the current is $1 . 5A$.

Hence, the voltage difference across the points is

${V}_{A} - {V}_{B} = \left(4 \times 1 . 5\right) - \left(2 \times 1 . 5\right) = 3V$

Different combination of $3$ resistors of equal resistance $R$ are shown in the figures. The increasing order for power dissipation is:

(A)

(B)

(C)

(D)
questions.solution:
The resistances can be calculated as

${R}_{A} = R + \dfrac{R}{2} = \dfrac{3R}{2}$

For second circuit

$\dfrac{1}{{R}_{B}} = \dfrac{1}{2R} + \dfrac{1}{R} = \dfrac{3}{2R} ⇒ {R}_{B} = \dfrac{2R}{3}$

For third circuit

${R}_{C} = \dfrac{R}{3}$

For fourth circuit

${R}_{D} = 3R$

The formula for power is given by $P = {I}^{2}R$.

Clearly,

${P}_{D} > {P}_{A} > {P}_{B} > {P}_{C}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A potential ${V}_{0}$ is applied across a uniform wire of resistance $R .$ The power dissipation is ${P}_{1} .$ The wire is then cut into two equal halves and a potential of ${V}_{0}$ is applied across the length of each half. The total power dissipation across two wires is ${P}_{2} .$ The ratio of ${P}_{2}: {P}_{1}$ is $\sqrt{x}: 1 .$ The value of $x$ is _____.
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the power dissipated in the first case can be written as

${P}_{1} = {V}_{0}^{2}R . . . \left(1\right)$

When the wire is halved, its resistance will also become half the previous value.

Thus, the formula to calculate the power dissipated in the second case can be written as

$\begin{cases}{P}_{2} & = & {V}_{0}^{2}\dfrac{R}{2} \times 2 \\ & = & \dfrac{4{{V}_{0}}^{2}}{R} . . . \left(2\right)\end{cases}$

Divide equation (2) by equation (1) to calculate the required ratio.

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{{P}_{2}}{{P}_{1}} & = & \dfrac{\dfrac{4{{V}_{0}}^{2}}{R}}{\dfrac{{{V}_{0}}^{2}}{R}} \\ & = & 4 \\ & = & \sqrt{16}\end{cases}$

Hence, $x = 16$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When a resistance of $5Ω$ is shunted with a moving coil galvanometer, it shows a full scale deflection for a current of $250mA,$ however when $1050Ω$ resistance is connected with it in series, it gives full scale deflection for $25$ volt. The resistance of galvanometer is$_________Ω .$
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the maximum current through the galvanometer, when a shunt resistance ${r}_{1}$ is connected is given by${\left({i}_{G}\right)}_{max} = \dfrac{{r}_{1}}{{r}_{1} + {R}_{G}}{i}_{max} . . . \left(1\right)$

When a series resistance ${r}_{2}$ is connected, the potential difference across the galvanometer is given by

$V = {\left({i}_{G}\right)}_{max}\left[{R}_{G} + {r}_{2}\right] . . . \left(2\right)$

From equations (1) and (2), it can be written that

$\begin{cases}V & = & \dfrac{{r}_{1}}{{r}_{1} + {R}_{G}}{i}_{max}\left({R}_{G} + {r}_{2}\right) \\ & ⇒ & V{r}_{1} + V{R}_{G} = {i}_{max}{r}_{1}{R}_{G} + {i}_{max}{r}_{1}{r}_{2} \\ & ⇒ & \left(V - {i}_{max}{r}_{1}\right){R}_{G} = {i}_{max}{r}_{1}{r}_{2} - V{r}_{1} \\ & ⇒ & {R}_{G} = \dfrac{{i}_{max}{r}_{1}{r}_{2} - V{r}_{1}}{V - {i}_{max}{r}_{1}} . . . \left(3\right)\end{cases}$

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (3) to calculate the required galvanometer resistance.

$\begin{cases}{R}_{G} & = & \dfrac{0 . 250A \times 5Ω \times 1050Ω - 25V \times 5Ω}{25V - 0 . 250A \times 5Ω} \\ & = & 50Ω\end{cases}$

The resistance of galvanometer is$_________Ω .$
questions.explanation:
The formula to calculate the maximum current through the galvanometer, when a shunt resistance ${r}_{1}$ is connected is given by${\left({i}_{G}\right)}_{max} = \dfrac{{r}_{1}}{{r}_{1} + {R}_{G}}{i}_{max} . . . \left(1\right)$

When a series resistance ${r}_{2}$ is connected, the potential difference across the galvanometer is given by

$V = {\left({i}_{G}\right)}_{max}\left[{R}_{G} + {r}_{2}\right] . . . \left(2\right)$

From equations (1) and (2), it can be written that

$\begin{cases}V & = & \dfrac{{r}_{1}}{{r}_{1} + {R}_{G}}{i}_{max}\left({R}_{G} + {r}_{2}\right) \\ & ⇒ & V{r}_{1} + V{R}_{G} = {i}_{max}{r}_{1}{R}_{G} + {i}_{max}{r}_{1}{r}_{2} \\ & ⇒ & \left(V - {i}_{max}{r}_{1}\right){R}_{G} = {i}_{max}{r}_{1}{r}_{2} - V{r}_{1} \\ & ⇒ & {R}_{G} = \dfrac{{i}_{max}{r}_{1}{r}_{2} - V{r}_{1}}{V - {i}_{max}{r}_{1}} . . . \left(3\right)\end{cases}$

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (3) to calculate the required galvanometer resistance.

$\begin{cases}{R}_{G} & = & \dfrac{0 . 250A \times 5Ω \times 1050Ω - 25V \times 5Ω}{25V - 0 . 250A \times 5Ω} \\ & = & 50Ω\end{cases}$

questions.q: A wire of resistance $160 Ω$ is melted and drawn in a wire of one-fourth of its length. The new resistance of the wire will be
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the resistance of the original wire is given by

$R = ρ\dfrac{l}{A} . . . \left(1\right)$

When the new wire is formed, its resistance is given by

$R ' = ρ\dfrac{l '}{4A} . . . \left(2\right)$

Divide equation (2) by equation (1) and simplify to obtain the expression for the new resistance.

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{R '}{R} & = & \dfrac{ρ\dfrac{l '}{4A}}{ρ\dfrac{l}{A}} \\ & ⇒ & R ' = R\dfrac{l '}{4l} . . . \left(3\right)\end{cases}$

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (3) to calculate the required new resistance.

$\begin{cases}R ' & = & \dfrac{\dfrac{l}{4}}{4l} \times 160Ω \\ & = & 10Ω\end{cases}$

questions.q: The current flowing through a conductor connected across a source is $2A$ and $1 . 2A$ at ${0}^{o}C$ and ${100}^{o}C$ respectively. The current flowing through the conductor at ${50}^{o}C$ will be _____ $\times {10}^{2}mA$.
questions.solution:
By Ohm's law, $V = IR$.

Let the current and resistance at $0 ° C$ be ${i}_{0} \text{ and } {R}_{0}$ respectively.

Let the current and resistance at $100 ° C$ be ${i}_{100} \text{ and } {R}_{100}$ respectively.

By the given condition,

${i}_{0}{R}_{0} = {i}_{100}{R}_{100} ⇒ 2{R}_{0} = 1 . 2{R}_{0} ( 1 + 100\alpha ) ⇒ 1 + 100\alpha = \dfrac{5}{3} ⇒ 50\alpha = \dfrac{1}{3}$

Since the voltage remains constant,

${i}_{50}{R}_{50} = {i}_{0}{R}_{0} ⇒ {i}_{50} = \dfrac{{i}_{0}{R}_{0}}{{R}_{50}} = \dfrac{2 \times {R}_{0}}{{R}_{0}\left(1 + 50\alpha\right)} = \dfrac{2}{1 + \dfrac{1}{3}} = 1 . 5A ⇒ {i}_{50} = 15 \times {10}^{2}mA$
questions.question: The current flowing through a conductor connected across a source is $2A$ and $1 . 2A$ at ${0}^{o}C$ and ${100}^{o}C$ respectively. The current flowing through the conductor at ${50}^{o}C$ will be _____ $\times {10}^{2}mA$.
questions.explanation:
By Ohm's law, $V = IR$.

Let the current and resistance at $0 ° C$ be ${i}_{0} \text{ and } {R}_{0}$ respectively.

Let the current and resistance at $100 ° C$ be ${i}_{100} \text{ and } {R}_{100}$ respectively.

By the given condition,

${i}_{0}{R}_{0} = {i}_{100}{R}_{100} ⇒ 2{R}_{0} = 1 . 2{R}_{0} ( 1 + 100\alpha ) ⇒ 1 + 100\alpha = \dfrac{5}{3} ⇒ 50\alpha = \dfrac{1}{3}$

Since the voltage remains constant,

${i}_{50}{R}_{50} = {i}_{0}{R}_{0} ⇒ {i}_{50} = \dfrac{{i}_{0}{R}_{0}}{{R}_{50}} = \dfrac{2 \times {R}_{0}}{{R}_{0}\left(1 + 50\alpha\right)} = \dfrac{2}{1 + \dfrac{1}{3}} = 1 . 5A ⇒ {i}_{50} = 15 \times {10}^{2}mA$

questions.q: Two identical cells each of emf $1 . 5V$ are connected in series across a $10Ω$ resistance. An ideal voltmeter connected across $10Ω$ resistance reads $1 . 5V$. The internal resistance of each cell is _____ $Ω$.
questions.solution:
Let ${R}_{1} = 10Ω$.

Using $V = iR$

$i = \left(\dfrac{3}{10 + 2r}\right)$

The voltmeter reading is $V ' = 1 . 5V$.

Thus,
$i{R}_{1} = V ' ⇒ 10 \times \dfrac{3}{10 + 2r} = 1 . 5$
$⇒ 20 = 10 + 2r$
$⇒ 2r = 10$
$⇒ r = 5Ω$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two identical heater filaments are connected first in parallel and then in series. At the same applied voltage, the ratio of heat produced in same time for parallel to series will be:
questions.solution:
Let the resistance of the filaments be $R$ and the voltage be $V$.

For the series combination the power is

${P}_{1} = \left(\dfrac{{V}^{2}}{2R}\right)$

For parallel combination,

${P}_{2} = \dfrac{{V}^{2}}{\left(\dfrac{R}{2}\right)} = \left(\dfrac{2{V}^{2}}{R}\right)$

Hence, the ratio is

$⇒ \dfrac{{P}_{2}}{{P}_{1}} = \dfrac{4}{1}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The current sensitivity of moving coil galvanometer is increased by $25 %$. This increase is achieved only changing in the number of turns of coils and area of cross section of the wire while keeping the resistance of galvanometer coil constant. The percentage change in the voltage sensitivity will be:
questions.solution:
The current sensitivity is given as

${S}_{i} = \dfrac{NBA}{C}$.

The voltage sensitivity is

${S}_{v} = \left(\dfrac{NAB}{CR}\right)$, where $R$ is the galvanometer resistance.

Since the resistance is constant,
$\Delta{S}_{i} = \left(\Delta{S}_{v}\right)$

Hence, the percentage change in voltage sensitivity is,

$\left(\Delta{S}_{v}\right) = + 25 %$.

questions.q: In the circuit diagram shown in figure given below, the current flowing through resistance $3Ω$ is $\dfrac{x}{3}A$. The value of $x$ is ________.
questions.solution:
Let the current flowing through the circuit be $IA$ in anti-clockwise direction.

The net resistance is $R = 4 . 5Ω + 2Ω + 1 . 5Ω = 8Ω$

Hence, $I = \dfrac{V}{R} = \dfrac{4V}{8Ω} = 0 . 5A$

The current flowing through the $3Ω$ resistor is

$\dfrac{6}{6 + 3} \times 0 . 5 = \dfrac{1}{3}A$

So, $x = 1$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a metallic conductor, under the effect of applied electric field, the free electrons of the conductor
options: Drift from higher potential to lower potential
Move with the uniform velocity throughout from lower potential to higher potential
Move in the straight line paths in the same direction
Move in the curved paths from lower potential to higher potential
questions.solution:
The electrons inside the conductor move with an average velocity due to the applied field in a direction opposite to the field, this velocity is known as drift velocity. Electric field are applied from high to low potential region of the conductor. Also, electrons are negatively charged.

Electron drifts from lower potential to higher potential on curved path.

questions.solution:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: $10$ resistors each of resistance $10 Ω$ can be connected in such as to get maximum and minimum equivalent resistance. The ratio of maximum and minimum equivalent resistance will be________.
questions.solution:
When all the resistors are connected in series, the total resistance is

${R}_{max} = 10R$

$⇒ {R}_{max} = 10 \times 10 = 100Ω$

When all the resistors are connected in parallel, the total resistance is

${R}_{min} = \dfrac{R}{10}$

$⇒ {R}_{min} = \dfrac{10}{10} = 1Ω$

Hence, the ratio,

$\dfrac{{R}_{max}}{{R}_{min}} = \dfrac{100Ω}{1Ω} = 100$.

questions.q: The number density of free electrons in copper is nearly $8 \times {10}^{28}{m}^{- 3}$. A copper wire has its area of cross-section $= 2 \times {10}^{- 6}{m}^{2}$ and is carrying a current of $3 . 2A$. The drift speed of the electrons is _____$\times {10}^{- 6}m{s}^{- 1}$.
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the current through any conductor is given by

$I = nAe{v}_{d} . . . \left(1\right)$

Substitute the values of the given parameters into equation (1) and solve to calculate the required drift velocity of the electrons.

$\begin{cases}3 . 2 & = & 8 \times {10}^{28} \times 2 \times {10}^{- 6} \times 1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 19} \times {v}_{d} \\ & ⇒ & {v}_{d} = \dfrac{3 . 2}{16 \times 1 . 6 \times 1000}m{s}^{- 1} \\ & = & 125 \times {10}^{- 6}m{s}^{- 1}\end{cases}$

questions.q: A student is provided with a variable voltage source $V$, a test resistor ${R}_{T} = 10Ω$, two identical galvanometers ${G}_{1}$ and ${G}_{2}$ and two additional resistors, ${R}_{1} = 10MΩ$ and ${R}_{2} = 0 . 001Ω$. For conducting an experiment to verify ohm's law, the most suitable circuit is:
questions.solution:
A galvanometer is a tool used to either detect or quantify an electric current. The movement of a magnetic needle or a coil in a magnetic field, which is an essential component of a galvanometer, typically indicates the current and its strength.

Depending up on the resistance and the connectivity in the circuit, galvanometer can be used either as voltmeter or as an ammeter.

Voltmeter should have very high resistance, while ammeter should be having very less resistance.

Hence, the high resistor ${R}_{1}$ should be connected in series with the galvanometer in order to measure the potential difference across the test resistor. Also, the low resistor ${R}_{2}$ should be connected in parallel with the galvanometer in order to measure the current across the test resistor.

Thus, this combination will work properly.

questions.q: Figure shows a part of an electric circuit. The potentials at points $a, b$ and $c$ are $30V, 12V$ and $2V$ respectively. The current through the $20Ω$ resistor will be,
questions.solution:
Let the potential be $xV$ at the junction.

By using $V = IR$ we get,

$30 - x = 10{i}_{1}x - 12 = 20{i}_{2}x - 2 = 30{i}_{3}$

By using Kirchhoff's law,

${i}_{1} = {i}_{2} + {i}_{3}$

$⇒ \dfrac{30 - x}{10} + \dfrac{12 - x}{20} + \dfrac{2 - x}{30} = 0 ⇒ \dfrac{90 - 3x + 18 - 1 . 5x + 2 - x}{30} = 0$

$⇒ x = 20V$

The current through the $20Ω$ resistor is

${i}_{2} = \left(\dfrac{30 - 12}{20}\right)A$

$⇒ {i}_{2} = \dfrac{8}{20}A = 0 . 4A$

questions.q: As shown in the figure the voltmeter reads $2V$ across $5Ω$ resistor. The resistance of the voltmeter is _____ $Ω$
questions.solution:
Let the resistance of the voltmeter be $RΩ$. The voltmeter is in parallel with the $5Ω$. So the total resistance in the circuit is

$\left(\dfrac{5R}{5 + R} + 2\right)Ω$

Applying Ohm's law in the whole circuit, $V = IR$,

$I = \left(\dfrac{3}{2 + \dfrac{5R}{5 + R}}\right)A$

It is given that the potential difference across $5Ω$ is $2V$.

Thus, by Ohm's law,

$\left(\dfrac{3}{2 + \dfrac{5R}{5 + R}}\right) \times \left(\dfrac{5R}{R + 5}\right) = 2 ⇒ \dfrac{15 + 3R}{10 + 7R} \times \dfrac{5R}{5 + R} = 2 ⇒ 15R = 20 + 14R ⇒ R = 20Ω$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Given below are two statements : One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.

Assertion A : For measuring the potential difference across a resistance of $600Ω$, the voltmeter with resistance $1000Ω$ will be preferred over voltmeter with resistance $4000Ω$.

Reason R : Voltmeter with higher resistance will draw smaller current than voltmeter with lower resistance.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
options: A is not correct but R is correct
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is correct but R is not correct
questions.solution:
Voltmeter is connected in parallel, so it should have very high resistance as to measure the potential difference, all the current should pass through the resistor and no current should pass through voltmeter for precise readings.
The current will divide and travel through the voltmeter if the voltmeter has a low resistance and will then give faulty readings.

Thus, A is not correct but R is correct.

questions.q: Equivalent resistance between the adjacent corners of a regular $n$-sided polygon of uniform wire of resistance $R$ would be :
questions.solution:
Given the total resistance of the wire is $R$. If the polygon has $n$ numbers of side, then the resistance $\left(r\right)$, as shown in the following figure, of each side can be written as

$r = \dfrac{R}{n} . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ( 1 )$

Among all the resistances, $\left(n - 1\right)$ resistances are connected in series combination, whereas, their equivalent resistance is connected in parallel with the ${n}^{th}$ resistance. The equivalent circuit diagram for the above set of resistances can be depicted as follows:

From the above equivalent circuit diagram, the net equivalent resistance $\left({R}_{eq}\right)$ for the entire combination can be calculated as follows-

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{1}{{R}_{eq}} & = & \dfrac{1}{\left(n - 1\right)r} + \dfrac{1}{r} \\ & = & \dfrac{1}{\left(n - 1\right)\dfrac{R}{n}} + \dfrac{1}{\dfrac{R}{n}} \\ & = & \dfrac{n}{\left(n - 1\right)R} + \dfrac{n}{R} \\ & = & \dfrac{{n}^{2}}{\left(n - 1\right)R} \\ {R}_{eq} & = & \dfrac{\left(n - 1\right)R}{{n}^{2}}\end{cases}$

Hence, the value of $x = 25$.

questions.q: The drift velocity of electrons for a conductor connected in an electrical circuit is ${V}_{d}$. The conductor is now replaced by another conductor with same material and same length but double the area of cross-section. The applied voltage remains same. The new drift velocity of electrons will be
questions.solution:
Drift velocity of electrons through a conductor kept in an external electric field is given by ${V}_{d} = - \dfrac{eE}{m}τ = - \dfrac{eV}{ml}τ$

Where, $e =$magnitude of charge on electron, $m =$mass of electron, $E =$external electric field and $τ =$average relaxation time.

As, drift velocity is independent of area. So, the new drift velocity of electrons will be ${V}_{d}$.

Let $r$ be the internal resistance of each cell.

In above shown figure, first represents the series connection of cells. Second and third figures represents the parallel connection of cells.

Now, in case of series connection, ${ε}_{net} = 2εand{r}_{net} = 2r$. So, current $i = \dfrac{2ε}{5 + 2r}$ .....(1)

In case of parallel connection, ${ε}_{net} = \dfrac{εr + εr}{r + r} = εand{r}_{net} = \dfrac{r}{2}$. So, current $i = \dfrac{ε}{\dfrac{r}{2} + 5}$ .....(2)

Equating (1) and (2), we get

$⇒ r + 10 = 5 + 2r$

$⇒ r = 5Ω$.

questions.q: The charge flowing in a conductor changes with time as $Q\left(t\right) = \alphat - \beta{t}^{2} + \gamma{t}^{3}$, where $\alpha, \beta$ and $\gamma$ are constants. Minimum value of current is:
questions.solution:
Given here, $Q = \left(\alphat - \beta{t}^{2} + \gamma{t}^{3}\right)$

Current flowing through conductor is given by

$i = \dfrac{d Q}{d t} = \left(\alpha - 2\betat + 3\gamma{t}^{2}\right) . . . \left(1\right)$

For current to be minimum, $\dfrac{d i}{d t} = 0$

So, $\dfrac{d i}{d t} = \left(6\gammat - 2\beta\right) = 0$

$⇒ t = \dfrac{\beta}{3\gamma}$

Substituting in equation (1),

$i = \left(\alpha - 2\betat + 3\gamma{t}^{2}\right) = \alpha - 2\beta\left(\dfrac{\beta}{3\gamma}\right) + 3\gamma{\left(\dfrac{\beta}{3\gamma}\right)}^{2} = \alpha - 2\dfrac{{\beta}^{2}}{3\gamma} + 3\dfrac{{\beta}^{2}}{9\gamma} = \left(\alpha - \dfrac{{\beta}^{2}}{3\gamma}\right)$

questions.q:
With the help of potentiometer, we can determine the value of emf of a given cell. The sensitivity of the potentiometer is

(A) directly proportional to the length of the potentiometer wire

(B) directly proportional to the potential gradient of the wire

(C) inversely proportional to the potential gradient of the wire

(D) inversely proportional to the length of the potentiometer wire

Choose the correct option for the above statements:
questions.solution:
The basic principle of the potentiometer is that the potential drop across any section of the wire will be directly proportional to the length of the wire, provided the wire is of the uniform cross-sectional area and a uniform current flows through the wire.

Therefore, sensitivity of potentiometer wire is inversely proportional to potential gradient.

$Sensitivity ∝ \dfrac{1}{\dfrac{V}{l}} ∝ \dfrac{l}{V}$

questions.q: Ratio of thermal energy released in two resistor $R$ and $3R$ connected in parallel in an electric circuit is :
questions.solution:
In parallel connection, potential difference across resistors remains the same.

Thermal energy released in resistor is given by $H = \dfrac{{V}^{2}}{R} \times t$

So, the ratio is $\dfrac{{H}_{1}}{{H}_{2}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{{V}^{2}t}{R}}{\dfrac{{V}^{2}t}{3R}} = \dfrac{3R}{R} = 3: 1$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The resistance of a wire is $5Ω$. Its new resistance in ohm, if stretched to $5$ times of its original length will be :
questions.solution:
The resistance of a wire $( R )$ is related to its resistivity $\left(ρ\right)$, length$( l )$ and cross-sectional area $\left(A\right)$ as:

$R = ρ\dfrac{l}{A}$

As the length of wire increases, the cross-sectional area decreases. The cross-sectional area in terms of volume $( V )$ and length $( l )$ is

$A = \dfrac{V}{l}$

$∴ R = ρ\dfrac{{l}^{2}}{V}$

Taking the volume of wire constant,

$R ∝ {l}^{2}$

So if ${R}^{'}$ is the resistance of wire after getting redrawn and $R$ is the initial resistance of wire,

$∴ \dfrac{{R}^{'}}{R} = \dfrac{( 5l{)}^{2}}{{l}^{2}} = 25 ⇒ {R}^{'} = 25 \times R = 125Ω$

questions.q: A uniform metallic wire carries a current $2A$, when $3 . 4V$ battery is connected across it. The mass of uniform metallic wire is $8 . 92 \times {10}^{- 3}kg$, density is $8 . 92 \times {10}^{3}kg{m}^{- 3}$ and resistivity is $1 . 7 \times {10}^{- 8}Ω - m$  The length of wire is :
questions.solution:
Given here, $I = 2A, V = 3 . 4V, m = 8 . 92 \times {10}^{- 3}kg,$

$d = 8 . 92 \times {10}^{3}kg{m}^{- 3}andρ = 1 . 7 \times {10}^{- 8}Ω - m$

From Ohm's law, resistance is $R = \dfrac{V}{I} = \dfrac{3 . 4}{2} = 1 . 7Ω$

As resistance of wire is given by $R = \dfrac{ρl}{A}$, where, $A$ is area and $l$ is length of wire.

$⇒ 1 . 7 = \dfrac{ρl}{A}$⇒ l = \dfrac{1 . 7A}{ρ}$

Now, volume$= \dfrac{m}{d} = \dfrac{8 . 92 \times {10}^{- 3}}{8 . 92 \times {10}^{3}} = {10}^{- 6}{m}^{3}$

Thus,

${l}^{2} = \dfrac{1 . 7A}{ρ} \times l = \dfrac{1 . 7\left(\dfrac{\text{volume}}{l}\right)}{ρ} \times l = \dfrac{1 . 7}{ρ}\left({10}^{- 6}\right) = \dfrac{1 . 7}{1 . 7 \times {10}^{- 8}} \times {10}^{- 6}$

Hence, $l = 10m$

questions.q: If a copper wire is stretched to increase its length by $20 %$. The percentage increase in resistance of the wire is _____%.
questions.solution:
Before heating, resistance of wire is ${R}_{0} = \left(\dfrac{ρ{l}_{0}}{{A}_{0}}\right)$

After heating, resistance is $R = \dfrac{ρl}{A}$

As volume = constant

Therefore,

${A}_{0}{l}_{0} = 1 . 2{l}_{0}A$

$⇒ A = \left(\dfrac{{A}_{0}}{1 . 2}\right)$

So,

$R = \dfrac{ρl}{A} = \dfrac{ρ \times \left(1 . 2{l}_{0}\right)}{\left(\dfrac{{A}_{0}}{1 . 2}\right)} = \dfrac{ρ{l}_{0}}{{A}_{0}} \times 1 . 44 = 1 . 44{R}_{0}$

Percentage increase in $R$= \dfrac{R - {R}_{0}}{{R}_{0}} \times 100 = 44 %$

questions.q:
A hollow cylindrical conductor has length of $3 . 14m$, while its inner and outer diameters are $4mm$ and $8mm$ respectively. The resistance of the conductor is $n \times {10}^{- 3}Ω$.
If the resistivity of the material is $2 . 4 \times {10}^{- 8}Ωm$. The value of $n$ is _____.
questions.solution:
Resistance of a conductor with uniform cross-section is given by,

$R = ρ\dfrac{l}{A}$

In this case the cross-sectional area is $\pi\left({b}^{2} - {a}^{2}\right)$.

Therefore,

$R = ρ\dfrac{l}{\pi\left({b}^{2} - {a}^{2}\right)} = \dfrac{\left(2 . 4 \times {10}^{- 8}\right) \times 3 . 14}{3 . 14 \times \left[\left({4}^{2} - {2}^{2}\right) \times {10}^{- 6}\right]} = 2 \times {10}^{- 3}Ω$

Hence, $n = 2$.

questions.q: A $1m$ long wire is broken into two unequal parts $X$ and $Y$. The $X$ part of the wire is stretched into another wire $W$. Length of $W$ is twice the length of $X$ and the resistance of $W$ is twice that of $Y$. Find the ratio of length of $X$ and$Y$.
questions.solution:
​​​​​​​

Resistance of a wire is given by $R = \dfrac{ρL}{A}$, where, $ρ$ is conductivity, $L$ is length of wire and $A$ is cross-sectional area of wire.

For a single wire, $A$ and $ρ$ are constant.

Thus, for parts $X$ and $Y$, resistance, $\dfrac{{R}_{X}}{{R}_{Y}} = \dfrac{{l}_{X}}{{l}_{Y}}$.

When wire is stretched to double of its length, then resistance becomes four times, thus, ${R}_{W} = 4{R}_{X} = 2{R}_{Y}$.

Hence, the ratio is $\dfrac{{R}_{X}}{{R}_{Y}} = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

So, $\dfrac{{l}_{X}}{{l}_{Y}} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : A uniform wire of resistance $80Ω$ is cut into four equal parts. These parts are now connected in parallel. The equivalent resistance of the combination will be $5Ω$.

Statement II : Two resistance $2R$ and $3R$ are connected in parallel in an electric circuit. The value of thermal energy developed in $3R$ and $2R$ will be in the ratio $3: 2$.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
options: Both statement I and statement II are correct
Both statement I and statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct.
questions.solution:
Statement $1 -$ $R = 80Ω$

When it is cut into $4$ equal parts, the resistance of each part will be,

${R}_{1} = {R}_{2} = {R}_{3} = {R}_{4} = 20Ω$

When these resistances are connected in parallel,

${R}_{eq} = \dfrac{20}{4} = 5Ω$

Hence, the statement I is correct.

Statement 2 -

When the resistances are connected in parallel, the potential difference between them is same. Therefore, the power consumed can be written as,

$P = \dfrac{{V}^{2}}{R}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{P}_{1}}{{P}_{2}} = \left(\dfrac{{R}_{2}}{{R}_{1}}\right) = \dfrac{2}{3}$

Hence, statement II is incorrect.

questions.q: An electrical bulb rated $220V, 100W$, is connected in series with another bulb rated $220V$, $60W$. If the voltage across combination is $220V$, the power consumed by the $100W$ bulb will be about _____ $W$.
questions.solution:
Electric power is given by $P = \dfrac{{V}^{2}}{R}$, here, $V$ is voltage and $R$ is resistance.

Now, for each bulb, ${R}_{1} = \dfrac{{V}^{2}}{P} = \dfrac{{220}^{2}}{100} = 484Ω$ and ${R}_{2} = \dfrac{{V}^{2}}{P} = \dfrac{{220}^{2}}{60} = 484\left(\dfrac{10}{6}\right)Ω$

Net current through the series combination is $I = \dfrac{220}{484 + 484 \times \dfrac{10}{6}}A = 0 . 171A$

Hence, the power consumed by the $100W$ bulb is ${P}_{1} = {I}^{2}{R}_{1} = 14 . 06W$

questions.q: A wire of resistance ${R}_{1}$R_{1}$ is drawn out so that its length is increased by twice of its original length. The ratio of new resistance to original resistance is:
questions.solution:
As per the given question, the change in the length is $∆ l = 2l$.

Resistance of a wire is given by, $R = \dfrac{ρl}{A}$

Therefore, ${R}_{1} = ρ\dfrac{{l}_{1}}{{A}_{1}}$

When the length is starched by $2{l}_{1}$, final length will be ${l}_{2} = {l}_{1} + 2{l}_{1} = 3{l}_{1}$. As the volume remains constant ${l}_{2}{A}_{2} = {l}_{1}{A}_{1} ⇒ {A}_{2} = \dfrac{{A}_{1}}{3}$. Therefore,

${R}_{2} = ρ\left(\dfrac{3{l}_{1}}{\dfrac{{A}_{1}}{3}}\right) = 9ρ\dfrac{{l}_{1}}{{A}_{1}}$

$∴ \dfrac{{R}_{2}}{{R}_{1}} = 9$

A. The drift velocity of electrons decreases with the increase in the temperature of conductor.
B. The drift velocity is inversely proportional to the area of cross-section of given conductor.
C. The drift velocity does not depend on the applied potential difference to the conductor.
D. The drift velocity of electron is inversely proportional to the length of the conductor.
E. The drift velocity increases with the increase in the temperature of conductor.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Drift velocity $= \left(\dfrac{eτ}{m}\right)E$

${v}_{d} = \left(\dfrac{eτ}{m}\right)\left(\dfrac{\DeltaV}{l}\right)$

$\DeltaV =$ Potential difference applied across the wire As temperature increases, relaxation time decreases, hence ${V}_{d}$ decreases.
As per formula, ${V}_{d} ∝ \dfrac{1}{l}$

${v}_{d} = \dfrac{I}{neA}$, as it is not mentioned that current is at steady state neither it is mentioned that $n$ is constant for given conductor. So it can't be said that ${v}_{d}$ is inversely proportional to $A$.

$I = neA{v}_{d} = \dfrac{V}{R} = \dfrac{V}{ρl}A$

${v}_{d} = \dfrac{eEτ}{m}$

$τ$ decrease with temperature increase.

First and fourth statements are correct.

${v}_{d} = \dfrac{V}{ρlne}\left(E = \dfrac{V}{l}\right)$

The length of the null point for cell of emf $20mV$ is found to be $60cm$. The resistance of the potentiometer wire is _____ $Ω$.
questions.solution:
Let resistance of potentiometers wire is $R$, then the current through $AB$

${i}_{AB} = \dfrac{4}{R + 780}$

Potential difference across $AB$

${V}_{AB} = \dfrac{4R}{R + 780}$

Potential difference across $AC$

${V}_{AC} = {V}_{AB}\dfrac{l}{L} = \dfrac{4R}{\left(R + 780\right)} \times \dfrac{60}{300} = \dfrac{4R}{5\left(R + 780\right)}$

This should be equal to $20mV$

$⇒ \dfrac{4R}{5\left(R + 780\right)} = 20 \times {10}^{- 3} = 2 \times {10}^{- 2}$

$⇒ 4R = {10}^{- 1}\left(R + 780\right)$

$⇒ 4R - \dfrac{R}{10} = 78$

$⇒ \dfrac{39R}{10} = 78$

$⇒ R = 20Ω$

questions.q: Resistance are connected in a meter bridge circuit as shown in the figure. The balancing length ${l}_{1}$ is $40cm$. Now an unknown resistance $x$ is connected in series with $P$ and new balancing length is found to be $80cm$ measured from the same end. Then the value of $x$ will be _____ $Ω$.
questions.solution:
Applying balanced condition for meter bridge

Initially, $\dfrac{P}{Q} = \dfrac{40cm}{60cm} = \dfrac{2}{3} . . . \left(1\right)

Finally, \dfrac{P + x}{Q} = \dfrac{80cm}{20cm} = \dfrac{4}{1}$ . . . $\left(2\right)$

Dividing equation $\left(2\right)$ by ($\left(1\right)$,

$\dfrac{P + x}{P} =$4 \times $\dfrac{3}{2} =$6$

$⇒ 1 + $\dfrac{x}{P} =$6 ⇒ $\dfrac{x}{P} =$5$

$∴ x = 5P = 5 \times 4 = 20Ω$

$

questions.q: In a potentiometer arrangement, a cell of emf $1 . 20V$ gives a balance point at $36cm$ length of wire. This cell is now replaced by another cell of emf $1 . 80V$. The difference in balancing length of potentiometer wire in above conditions will be _____ $cm$.
questions.solution:
In a potentiometer, null point or balance point is defined as the point where the deflection of the galvanometer is zero. If emf of the unknown battery is $ε$ then,

$ε =$(Potential Gradient)$\times$(Balancing length $l$). Therefore,

$\dfrac{{ε}_{1}}{{ε}_{2}} = \dfrac{{l}_{1}}{{l}_{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1 . 20}{1 . 80} = \dfrac{36}{{l}_{2}}$

$⇒ {l}_{2} = 18 \times 3 = 54cm$

Hence, difference in balancing length is ${l}_{2} - {l}_{1} = 54 - 36 = 18cm$

questions.q: Eight copper wire of length $l$ and diameter d are joined in parallel to form a single composite conductor of resistance $R$. If a single copper wire of length $2l$ have the same resistance $\left(R\right)$ then its diameter will be _____ $d$.
questions.solution:
Each wire has resistance, $r = ρ\dfrac{4l}{\pi{d}^{2}}$

Eight wire in parallel, then equivalent resistance is

$R = \dfrac{r}{8} = \dfrac{ρl}{2\pi{d}^{2}}$

Single copper wire of length $2l$ has resistance $R = ρ\dfrac{2l \times 4}{\pi{d}_{1}^{2}}$.

Comparing both equations, we get,

$ρ\dfrac{8l}{\pi{d}_{1}^{2}} = \dfrac{ρl}{2\pi{d}^{2}}$

$⇒ {d}_{1} = 4d$

questions.q: The combination of two identical cells, whether connected in series or parallel combination provides the same current through an external resistance of $2Ω$. The value of internal resistance of each cell is
questions.solution:
When the cells are connected in series ${i}_{s} = \dfrac{2ε}{2r + R} = \dfrac{2ε}{2r + 2}$

When they are connected in parallel, the emf is ${ε}_{p} = \dfrac{\dfrac{ε}{r} + \dfrac{ε}{r}}{\dfrac{1}{r} + \dfrac{1}{r}} = ε$ and the effective internal resistance will be ${r}_{p} = \dfrac{r \times r}{r + r} = \dfrac{r}{2}$. Therefore, the current will be,

${i}_{p} = \dfrac{ε}{R + \dfrac{r}{2}} = \dfrac{ε}{2 + \dfrac{r}{2}} = \dfrac{2ε}{4 + r}$

Since, ${i}_{s} = {i}_{p} ⇒ \dfrac{2ε}{2r + 2} = \dfrac{2ε}{4 + r} ⇒ r = 2Ω$
questions.question: The combination of two identical cells, whether connected in series or parallel combination provides the same current through an external resistance of $2Ω$. The value of internal resistance of each cell is
questions.explanation:
When the cells are connected in series ${i}_{s} = \dfrac{2ε}{2r + R} = \dfrac{2ε}{2r + 2}$

When they are connected in parallel, the emf is ${ε}_{p} = \dfrac{\dfrac{ε}{r} + \dfrac{ε}{r}}{\dfrac{1}{r} + \dfrac{1}{r}} = ε$ and the effective internal resistance will be ${r}_{p} = \dfrac{r \times r}{r + r} = \dfrac{r}{2}$. Therefore, the current will be,

${i}_{p} = \dfrac{ε}{R + \dfrac{r}{2}} = \dfrac{ε}{2 + \dfrac{r}{2}} = \dfrac{2ε}{4 + r}$

questions.q: Two resistors are connected in series across a battery as shown in figure. If a voltmeter of resistance $2000Ω$ is used to measure the potential difference across $500Ω$ resister, the reading of the voltmeter will be _____ $V$

questions.q: Two coils require $20$ minutes and $60$ minutes respectively to produce same amount of heat energy when connected separately to the same source. If they are connected in parallel arrangement to the same source; the time required to produce same amount of heat by the combination of coils, will be _____ $min$.
questions.solution:
If $H$ is the heat required to heat the water, then

${P}_{1} \times 60 = H ⇒ {P}_{1} = \dfrac{H}{60} and {P}_{2} \times 20 = H ⇒ {P}_{2} = \dfrac{H}{20}$

When the coils are connected in parallel their powers will get added. If the required time now is $t$, then

$\left({P}_{1} + {P}_{2}\right)t = H ⇒ t = \dfrac{H}{\dfrac{H}{60} + \dfrac{H}{20}} = 15min$

questions.q: All resistances in figure are $1Ω$ each. The value of current '$I$' is $\dfrac{a}{5}A$. The value of $a$ is _____ .
questions.solution:
Each pair on the right side of the circuit is in parallel connection, hence it can be replaced by a resistance of $\dfrac{r}{2}$ as shown.

Now, $r \text{ and } \dfrac{r}{2}$ in each branch on the right side is in series, hence combined resistance value will be, $\dfrac{3r}{2}$. Upper branch having resistance $\dfrac{3r}{2}$ is in parallel with another $\dfrac{3r}{2}$, hence it can be written as $\dfrac{3r}{4}$.

Further, simplified circuit will have net resistance of $\dfrac{7r}{8}$.

Therefore, ${R}_{eq} = \dfrac{7r}{8} + r = \dfrac{7}{8} + 1 = \dfrac{15}{8}Ω$

Now, current $I = \dfrac{3}{\dfrac{15}{8}} = \dfrac{8}{5}A$

Hence, value of $a = 8$.

questions.q: A meter bridge setup is shown in the figure. It is used to determine an unknown resistance $R$ using a given resistor of $15Ω$. The galvanometer $\left(G\right)$ shows null defection when tapping key is at $43cm$ mark from end $A$. If the end correction for end $A$ is $2cm$, then the determined value of $R$ will be $Ω$.
questions.solution:
Using the conditions of a balanced wheatstone bridge and adding the end correction.

$\dfrac{15}{R} = \dfrac{l + e}{\left(L + e\right) - \left(l + e\right)} ⇒ \dfrac{15}{\left(43 + 2\right)} = \dfrac{R}{\left(102 - 45\right)} ⇒ R = \dfrac{57}{45} \times 15$

$⇒ R = 19Ω$

questions.q: Current measured by the ammeter $\left(A\right)$ in the reported circuit when no current flows through $10Ω$ resistance, will be _____ $A$.
questions.solution:
This is a Wheatstone circuit. For the current to be zero in $10Ω$ the Wheatstone circuit should be balanced. Therefore,

$\dfrac{R}{3} = \dfrac{4}{6} ⇒ R = 2Ω$

Now, the equivalent resistance across the battery will be,

${R}_{eq} = \dfrac{\left(2 + 4\right) \times \left(3 + 6\right)}{\left(2 + 4\right) + \left(3 + 6\right)} = 3 . 6Ω$

Therefore, the current measured by the ammeter is $i = \dfrac{V}{R} = \dfrac{36}{3 . 6} = 10A$.

questions.q: In the given circuit 'a' is an arbitrary constant. The value of $m$ for which the equivalent circuit resistance is minimum, will be $\sqrt{\dfrac{x}{2}}$. The value of $x$ is _____ .
questions.solution:
Left part of the resistors are connected in parallel, hence ${R}_{1} = \dfrac{am}{3}$.

Similarly, for the right part of the resistors we can write, ${R}_{2} = \dfrac{a}{2m}$.

Therefore, equivalent resistance will be,

$R = \dfrac{am}{3} + \dfrac{a}{2m}$

Differentiating both sides w.r.t $m$ to observe critical points, we get $\dfrac{dR}{dm} = \dfrac{a}{3} + \dfrac{a\left(- 1\right)}{2{m}^{2}} = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{a}{3} = \dfrac{a}{2{m}^{2}}$⇒ m = \sqrt{\dfrac{3}{2}}$

Thus, $x = 3$.

Thus, $x = 3$.
